```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reindeer)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
has_dsp <- requireNamespace("superassp", quietly = TRUE)
# Work on a copy so the examples can write metadata freely.
src <- demo_corpus()@basePath
work <- tempfile("speaker_")
dir.create(work)
file.copy(src, work, recursive = TRUE)
corp <- corpus(file.path(work, basename(src)))
```

Formant and pitch trackers work best with settings that fit the speaker: a
child needs a higher formant ceiling than an adult man. reindeer picks those
settings from the speaker's **Age** and **Gender** metadata, using
literature-derived norms, and passes them to the signal-processing routine
under whatever name that routine uses.

## Put the speaker data where it belongs

Metadata lives at three levels, and the most specific one wins: **bundle**
(one recording) over **session** over **database** (defaults for everyone).

```{r levels}
set_metadata(corp, list(Project = "demo"))                          # database
set_metadata(corp, list(Age = 6, Gender = "Female"), session = "0000")  # session
set_metadata(corp, list(Age = 40, Gender = "Male"),
             session = "0000", bundle = "msajc003")                 # one bundle
get_metadata(corp) |> select(session, bundle, Age, Gender, Project)
```

## Preview what will be applied

`dsp_parameters()` shows the norms for a given age and gender, before any
measurement.

```{r preview}
dsp_parameters(age = c(6, 40), gender = c("Female", "Male")) |>
  select(Age, Gender, minF, maxF, numFormants, nominalF1, windowSize)
```

## Measure, and see the effect

```{r measure, eval = has_dsp}
vowels <- collect(query(corp, "Phonetic == V|@|i:|u:|o:|A:|E|I|O"))
f1 <- function(...) {
  as.numeric(quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, .at = 0.5, ...)$F1_Hz)
}
with_norms    <- suppressWarnings(f1())
without_norms <- suppressWarnings(f1(.use_metadata = FALSE))
summary(abs(with_norms - without_norms))   # Hz moved by the speaker settings
```

The measured F1 values really differ: the metadata changed the settings the
tracker ran with, not just a column in the output. Pass
`.use_metadata = FALSE` to measure every speaker with the routine's defaults,
or override a single setting for everyone, e.g.
`quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, nominalF1 = 500)`.

A routine that cannot receive any norm (a fixed-parameter tracker, say)
warns once per call so that you know the speaker data had no effect.

## Results are cached per recording

The expensive step is analysing a whole recording, so reindeer analyses each
file once and slices every segment out of the result. That table is cached;
asking again, for other time points or other segments of the same recordings,
is a cache hit.

```{r cache, eval = has_dsp}
invisible(suppressMessages(clear_cache(corp)))   # start cold
midpoint <- suppressWarnings(quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, .at = 0.5))
table(midpoint$.cache_status)           # first time: computed
quarter  <- suppressWarnings(quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, .at = 0.25))
table(quarter$.cache_status)            # different time point, same recordings
```

The cache is invalidated when the recording, the routine, or the speaker
settings change. Look at its size with `summary(corp)` and empty it with
`clear_cache(corp)` (or `clear_cache(corp, older_than = 30)`).

## Several time points and long form

`.at` takes several relative positions. `pivot_tracks_longer()` turns the
wide result into one row per segment, track and time point, ready for
plotting.

```{r pivot, eval = has_dsp}
contour <- suppressWarnings(
  quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, .at = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)))
long <- pivot_tracks_longer(contour, cols = c("F1_Hz", "F2_Hz"))
head(as.data.frame(long)[, c("labels", "bundle", "track", "rel_time", "value")], 6)
```
